judge_panel.reason: The paper uses 'SNR0' and 'SNR' interchangeably to refer to the same fixed value of 50 for the golden EMRI. For example, Eq. (17) defines the observability criterion as '(8/SNR_0)' and the abstract states 'detectable (∆ψgas > 8/SNR)' — both refer to SNR=SNR0=50. There is no distortion of the detectability criterion; the notation is simply used inconsistently but refers to the same numerical quantity throughout.

The paper uses the generic threshold as "a dephasing is observable if its more than 8/SNR ... where SNR is the signal-to-noise ratio of the source in the LISA band," and then specializes to the fiducial case with "SNR0 = 50" and "Λ = (|∆ψlin| + 2σ̂turb)/(8/SNR0)." This is a notation change from generic SNR to the specific fiducial SNR0, not an incorrect alteration of the criterion.

The paper correctly defines the general criterion as "8/SNR... where SNR is the signal-to-noise ratio of the source" and simply uses "SNR_0" to denote the specific value of 50 for their fiducial "golden" EMRI. The reviewer's claim misinterprets a straightforward notational choice as a substantive error.
